data.title: EASTERN PLATINUM LIMITED REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER OF 2026
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 13, 2026 /CNW/ -- Eastern Platinum Limited () () ("Eastplats" or the "Company") is pleased to report that it has filed its condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and the corresponding management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A"). Below is a summary of the Company's financial results for the third quarter of 2026 ("Q3 2026") and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 ("YTD 2026") in comparison to the same respective period in 2025 ("Q3 2025" and "YTD 2025") (all amounts in USD unless specified):

  • Revenue for Q3 2026 decreased to $13.5 million (Q3 2025 - $13.7 million), representing a -$0.2 million or 1.4% decrease. Revenue for YTD 2026 decreased to $35.2 million (YTD 2025 – $39.2 million), representing a $4 million or 10.2% decrease.
  • Mine operating loss increased by $0.2 million to -$0.49 million in Q3 2026 (Q3 2025 – $0.24 million) while gross margin decreased from -1.7% in Q3 2025 to -3.6% in Q3 2026. The decrease was mainly due to decrease in platinum-group-metal ("PGM") sales and higher production costs. Mine operating loss in YTD 2026 decreased by $0.5 million (or 10.9%) to mine operating loss of $4.0 million (YTD 2025 – $4.5 million), resulting from a slightly increased gross margin of -11.5% in YTD 2026 from -11.6% in YTD 2025.
  • Operating loss was $4.0 million in Q3 2026 compared to a loss of $3.4 million in Q3 2025, primarily due to lower mine operating loss and higher site service cost. Operating loss was $14.9 million in YTD 2026 compared to a loss of $14.5 million in YTD 2025.
  • Net loss attributable to equity shareholders was $2.8 million ($0.01 loss per share) in Q3 2026 versus net loss attributable to equity shareholders of $2.2 million ($0.01 loss per share) in Q3 2025. The increase in net loss was primarily due to the decrease in overall sales and higher production costs incurred at the CRM.
  • Net loss attributable to equity shareholders was $13.0 million ($0.06 loss per share) in YTD 2026 compared to net loss attributable to equity shareholders of $10.9 million ($0.05 loss per share) in YTD 2025. The decrease of YTD 2026 net income was mainly attributable to the same reasons as described above for the quarter.
  • The Company had a working capital deficit (current assets less current liabilities) of $71.4 million as at September 30, 2026 (December 31, 2025 – working capital deficit of $56.9 million) and short-term cash resources of $1,113,000 (consisting of cash and cash equivalents) (December 31, 2025 – $177,000).

Charlie Liu, Interim Chief Executive Officer and President of Eastplats commented, "We had a challenging third quarter as monthly run-of-mine processing tonnages at the Crocodile River Mine were lower than targeted. But we have seen some improvement in our operation results in this quarter as we have increased our underground hoisting capability."

Operations

The Company derived revenue from the processing of PGM and chrome concentrates at the CRM. Eastplats' majority of revenue (approximately 75% and 78% for Q3 2026 and YTD 2026) is from PGM concentrate sales to Impala Platinum Limited under related offtake agreements. This is in line with the Company's expectations as it continues to ramp up production at the CRM.

The Company started processing ROM UG2 ore from the Zandfontein underground section at the CRM during the third quarter of 2024, at higher grades of chrome and PGM recovery, respectively.

data.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman: Reuters
data.description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company’s leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.

Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.

On Thursday, November 12, Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry’s heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.

He apologised in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, whom the US was investigating for potentially spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related.

The New York Times earlier this week reported Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Huang had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia employee.

Teter did not respond to a request for comment. Wagonfeld did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for ex-CEO Huang and an Nvidia spokesperson declined to comment. A phone call and email to the contact information listed on a business card for Alice Huang went unanswered.

During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ones from 2025.

In two separate messages in October, Huang told Nvidia leaders, including Teter and Wagonfeld, that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers. In other messages, Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed.

Nvidia’s Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.

That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe as an affair, the people said. Ultimately, neither Nvidia nor Huang filed a lawsuit against the paper. A spokesperson for The New York Times said the paper received no legal demand.

It is unclear when his relationship with Alice Huang became intimate. Photos posted online and verified by Reuters show them together in the US, China and elsewhere, dating as far back as December 2023.

On November 10, the independent members of Nvidia’s board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after The New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Huang’s relations with Alice Huang, as well as US authorities’ suspicions that she was spying for China. Beijing has denied she is a spy.

Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government.

Jensen Huang said in an interview with Bloomberg published on October 29 that the US government had not informed him about its suspicions regarding Alice Huang.

Nvidia’s stock has fallen more than 30% since its October 6 closing high, erasing more than $1.8 trillion from its market capitalisation.

data.title: TVS Motor Steps Up Europe Push With Three Electric Scooters, RTR 125 At EICMA 2026
data.description:
The company showcased four production-ready models in Milan as it expands its European dealer network. The bigger objective is to build a business around local customers, products and after-sales support rather than rely on exports alone

TVS Motor Company's second appearance at EICMA was a more significant one than its debut last year. This time, the Indian manufacturer arrived in Milan with four production-ready models for European customers, a growing dealer network and, for the first time at the show, an opportunity for visitors to experience its products through test rides.

The line-up included three electric scooters, the Orbiter, M1-S and TVS X, alongside the RTR 125 motorcycle. Together, they cover different parts of the European two-wheeler market, from low-speed urban commuting and electric maxi-scooters to connected premium mobility and entry-level sports motorcycling.

But the more important development is what sits behind these products. TVS is gradually moving from announcing its European ambitions to building the retail, engineering and service infrastructure needed to support a long-term business in the region.

Europe Growth Strategy

TVS first used EICMA 2025 to outline its European ambitions. Since then, the company has worked on expanding its dealer network and improving customer support in the region. Italy, its first European market, now has more than 100 retailers. TVS says its sales in the country have increased by 110 per cent over the past year. It also has 22 retailers across Spain and Portugal, while France and Germany are identified as the next markets for expansion.

This is important because entering a market is only the first step for an automobile manufacturer. Building a dependable dealer and service network is what allows it to sell at scale, support customers after purchase and develop brand recognition over time.

TVS has also established a Global Centre of Excellence for Design and Engineering in Bologna, Italy. The facility gives the company a presence closer to European customers and markets, complementing its engineering and product development capabilities elsewhere.

The company has also set a larger international business target. Its latest post-EICMA communication says international operations could contribute up to 40 per cent of overall revenue by 2030. Europe is expected to play a role in that expansion, alongside TVS' other overseas markets.

Three Electric Scooters

The most noticeable part of the EICMA line-up was the electric portfolio. Rather than relying on one scooter to serve every customer, TVS has presented three products with different roles.

ModelPositioningKey details
TVS OrbiterEveryday city mobilityRemovable 1.8kWh or 3.1kWh batteries; expected WMTC range of 70km or 105km
TVS M1-SElectric maxi-scooter4.2kWh battery, 105km/h top speed, expected WMTC range of 120km
TVS XPremium connected electric scooter4.43kWh battery, 110km/h top speed, 10.2-inch touchscreen and LTE connectivity

The Orbiter is positioned as the practical city scooter. Its biggest differentiator is the choice of two removable battery packs, allowing customers to select the capacity according to their daily travel requirements. The 1.8kWh version has an expected range of 70km, while the 3.1kWh version is expected to cover up to 105km under the WMTC test cycle.

Both versions have a 45km/h top speed and a 34-litre under-seat storage compartment. The batteries can be removed for charging, which could be useful for people who do not have direct access to a charging point where they park.

The M1-S takes TVS into the electric maxi-scooter category. It uses a 4.2kWh battery and a motor producing 12.5kW of peak power, with a claimed top speed of 105km/h. The company estimates a range of 120km under the European WMTC test cycle.

Practicality is a key part of its positioning. The scooter gets 26 litres of under-seat storage designed to accommodate a full-face helmet. Its battery can charge from 10 per cent to 80 per cent in around 75 minutes using the 1.8kW charger. It also gets a seven-inch TFT display and onboard LTE connectivity.

The TVS X sits at the premium end of the electric range. It uses a 4.43kWh battery, has a claimed top speed of 110km/h and offers an expected range of up to 140km under internal test conditions. Its 10.2-inch touchscreen supports Android Auto, onboard navigation, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and an independent LTE connection.

The X is not just about the size of its display. It represents TVS' attempt to combine electric performance with connected features, an aluminium frame and a more technology-led ownership experience.

RTR 125 Gives TVS An Entry Point Into European Motorcycling

The fourth model, the TVS RTR 125, is the only petrol-powered motorcycle in the four-model line-up. It has a liquid-cooled 125cc, four-valve DOHC engine producing 11kW (14.9PS) and 12Nm of torque. The engine is paired with a six-speed gearbox and an assist-and-slipper clutch. It also gets a five-inch TFT display with Bluetooth connectivity and navigation mirroring, along with ride modes and dual-channel ABS.

The motorcycle has been developed for European A1 licence holders, a category that allows riders to operate motorcycles of up to 125cc and 11kW. This makes it an entry point for younger riders and first-time motorcycle buyers who may eventually consider larger TVS models.

The company's European motorcycle portfolio also includes the RR 310, RTR 310, Ronin and RTX 300. The RTX 300, which was shown at EICMA 2025, is also scheduled to reach European dealerships.

'82 Series Brings TVS Racing's History To Milan

Alongside the four production-ready models, TVS also presented the '82 Series Collection for the first time globally. It comprises four one-off concept motorcycles inspired by the company's motorsport history.

The collection includes the '82 Series RR 310, RTR 310, RTX 300 and Ronin 250. The RTR 310 concept, for instance, features cornering ABS, traction control and wheelie control supported by a six-axis IMU. The RTX 300 interpretation takes an adventure-focused approach, while the Ronin 250 combines neo-retro, scrambler and roadster elements. These are display concepts and not confirmed production models.

A European Business

TVS' EICMA line-up suggests that the company is looking at Europe through a broader lens. The Orbiter targets everyday city travel, the M1-S and TVS X address different parts of the electric scooter market, while the RTR 125 gives it an entry-level petrol motorcycle.

However, the four models are not all ready to reach dealerships immediately. The TVS X is undergoing European Whole Vehicle Type Approval, while the Orbiter's EU type approval is expected in 2027. TVS has said market-specific pricing, final specifications and availability dates will be announced closer to the respective launches.

For TVS, the next phase in Europe will be less about how many products it can display at EICMA and more about how quickly it can bring them to market, build customer confidence and support owners across different countries. The expanding dealer network is a start. The real test will be converting that presence into sustained sales.

data.title: Tata Motors PV Records Highest-Ever Quarterly Revenue Of Rs 96,920 Crore, Sales Grow 40%
data.description:
Consolidated revenue rose 34 per cent year-on-year to Rs 96,920 crore, while exceptional charges of Rs 6,700 crore pushed the company into a net loss; JLR also lowered its full-year financial guidance

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited (TMPVL) reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,500 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with a profit in the year-ago period. The loss was primarily driven by exceptional charges of Rs 6,700 crore, even as revenue increased 34 per cent year-on-year to Rs 96,920 crore.

The exceptional items mainly comprised provisions of Rs 3,800 crore towards employee separation costs and asset impairment of Rs 2,900 crore. Consequently, profit before tax (PBT) after exceptional items stood at a loss of Rs 6,300 crore. PBT before exceptional items was Rs 403 crore, while the net loss after recognition of a deferred tax asset stood at Rs 5,500 crore.

Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was Rs 5,995 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 6.2 per cent, an improvement of 630 basis points year-on-year. EBIT margin rose 790 basis points to 1.1 per cent. The improvement in the annual comparison was largely due to the recovery from the cyber incident that affected Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) during the corresponding quarter last year.

However, margins came under pressure sequentially due to an adverse product mix and continued commodity cost increases. Consolidated free cash flow was negative at Rs 6,300 crore, taking net debt to Rs 50,800 crore as of September 30, 2026.

JLR Cuts FY27 Guidance Amid Market Pressures

JLR reported revenue of £5.9 billion (British pound) for Q2 FY27, up 20.3 per cent year-on-year. EBITDA margin improved by 820 basis points to 6.6 per cent, while EBIT margin stood at 1.1 per cent, up 970 basis points. Profit before tax and exceptional items was £6 million (British pound), compared with a loss of £485 million (British pound) in the year-ago quarter.

The luxury vehicle maker, however, recorded exceptional charges of £530 million (British pound) during the quarter, related to restructuring activities, employee separation costs and write-downs of assets and intangible assets under development.

JLR reported a free cash outflow of £540 million (British pound), with a closing cash balance of £1.8 billion (British pound). Its total liquidity stood at £6 billion (British pound) as of September 30, including undrawn credit facilities and loans.

In view of market challenges, geopolitical risks and exceptional costs, JLR has revised its full-year FY27 guidance. It now expects an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3 per cent and free cash outflow of approximately £1.25 billion.

On the product front, JLR unveiled three electric models: the Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric and Jaguar Type 01. Deliveries are expected to begin in early 2027. The company also plans to launch the Range Rover GT and an all-electric Defender based on its new EMA architecture next year.

JLR said its Enterprise Missions programme remains on track to deliver £1.7 billion in savings over the next two years, with the objective of simplifying operations and reducing breakeven volumes towards 300,000 units.

Tata PV Posts Record Quarterly Revenue

Tata Passenger Vehicles recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 20,423 crore, growing 50.9 per cent year-on-year. Volumes increased 40 per cent during the quarter, significantly outperforming the industry, according to the company.

Despite the strong growth, the domestic passenger vehicle business reported an EBITDA margin of 4 per cent, down 180 basis points year-on-year, while EBIT margin stood at -0.3 per cent. The company attributed the margin pressure to higher commodity costs and foreign exchange impact.

Electric vehicle volumes grew 90 per cent year-on-year, while the company's EV market share stood at 43 per cent in Q2 FY27. Tata PV retained its second position in the overall passenger vehicle market, with a Vahan market share of 14.3 per cent.

Alternative powertrains accounted for more than 50 per cent of the company's sales during the quarter, with EVs contributing 23 per cent and CNG vehicles 28 per cent.

Tata PV reported positive free cash flow of Rs 825 crore for the quarter. Its closing cash balance stood at Rs 11,000 crore against gross debt of Rs 3,100 crore, resulting in net cash of Rs 7,900 crore.

During the quarter, the company introduced its new global consumer-facing brand identity, Tata.Cars. It also launched the Tata Aeris and introduced new editions of the Curvv and Sierra. The company extended its Battery-as-a-Service offering across its electric vehicle portfolio.

Looking ahead, the company said geopolitical developments, demand in the luxury vehicle segment, the pace of EV adoption and commodity costs would remain key factors to monitor. While the domestic business will focus on sustaining growth and improving margins through cost reductions and pricing actions, JLR's near-term priorities include building momentum for its new electric models and executing its Enterprise Missions plan.

data.title: Three fast-growing water infra stocks
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Water infrastructure is emerging as an important investment theme in India, with rising demand for clean drinking water, sewage treatment, and wastewater recycling.

Government initiatives, urbanization, and industrial expansion are creating opportunities for companies involved in water management and infrastructure development. Several listed companies are also expanding their project portfolios and reporting revenue and order-book growth.

However, the pace at which these projects translate into actual earnings will depend on execution, margins and timely payments.

In this editorial, we look at three fast-growing water infrastructure stocks and examine what is driving their growth and future business prospects.

The company is a water technology company specializing in drinking water treatment, sewage treatment, desalination, and wastewater recycling. It executes projects for municipal bodies and industrial customers in India and overseas.

VA Tech Wabag continues to grow rapidly.

While the company has grown sales at a 10% CAGR over the last three years, net profits have grown at a solid 222.7%. The outlook is promising because of the large order book. Recently, it crossed Rs.20,000 crore in order book for the first time ever.

The company says that growth is on track, driven by efficient execution and new projects. The company expects revenues to grow at 15-20% CAGR over the next few years, with a strong Ebitda margin of 13-15%.

In H1FY27, VA Tech Wabag secured two landmark "Mega" orders, a "Mega" SWRO project that marks its entry into Kuwait, and a "Mega" deal with Reliance Industries for one of the largest desalination plants in India at Jamnagar.

Together with its entry into the UAE through Ajman, expansion in Europe with Donauinsel Water Works, and key municipal orders from BWSSB and DJB, these wins showcase the trust its clients place in it for their most complex, technology-intensive projects.

In H1 FY27, the company reported strong margins and better working capital management that helped it deliver its 15th back-to-back quarter of positive net cash, which crossed Rs.1,100 crore excluding HAM, another major milestone for WABAG.

The management says that rising water security needs and the push on treated water reuse and desalination both for municipal and industrial sectors, are strong tailwinds for the sector. They will stay selective, focusing on securing more "Large" and "Mega", technology-led projects.

Next on the list is the stock of Enviro Infra Engineers.

The company is engaged in designing, construction, operation, and maintenance of Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) and Water Supply Scheme Projects (WSSPs). It also has a presence in the renewables space.

While the company has grown sales at a 57.3% CAGR over the last three years, net profits have grown at 50.4%.

The company has a large and diversified order book of approximately Rs.6,778 crore across water infrastructure and renewable energy, providing healthy revenue visibility.

Q2FY27 reflected strong growth in the company's operations, supported by continued execution across its core water and wastewater infrastructure business and the increasing contribution from the renewable energy portfolio.

During the quarter, revenue grew by 60% year-on-year, while Ebitda increased 15.3%, reflecting the growing scale and diversification of its business.

The core Water and Wastewater segment contributes around 71% of consolidated revenue, underscoring its significance to the overall business.

The company is in the advanced stages of completing three STP projects, namely, the 60 MLD STP at Mathura, the 77 MLD STP at Yamuna Nagar, and the 50 MLD STP at Amritsar, all being delivered well ahead of time.

The management says the focus is on strengthening execution capabilities, expanding its presence across sustainable infrastructure segments and creating long-term value for stakeholders.

The company is a top player in water and wastewater treatment, specializing in zero liquid discharge (ZLD) technology, with in-house expertise spanning design, R&D, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, operation & maintenance (O&M), and IoT-driven digital solutions.

While the company has grown sales at a 17.6% CAGR over the last three years, net profits have grown at 60.8%.

Moving ahead, Concord has taken initiatives to grow the business. In H1FY27, the company's H-Xtreme Heat Exchanger and the compressed biogas platform achieved their first order milestones during the period.

The company's dehumidification platform has also moved into action. The initiative is now operational, expanding the Company's addressable market across pharmaceuticals, food and beverages, batteries, solar manufacturing, and semiconductors.

As of 30 September 2026, the order book stands at Rs.716.40 crore.

The company says that with rising water scarcity, tighter environmental compliance and increasing adoption of water recycling solutions, India is expected to remain its principal growth market over the coming years.

India's water infrastructure sector is attracting attention as rising urbanisation, industrial demand, and government investment drive the need for better water supply, sewage treatment, and wastewater management.

Companies operating in this space could benefit from large-scale projects under government initiatives, including the Jal Jeevan Mission and Namami Gange.

However, investors should not confuse the opportunity with guaranteed earnings growth. Order book expansion, project execution, working capital requirements, and debt levels will determine how much of this demand translates into profits.

Investors should also be cautious about high valuations, delayed payments, and intense competition before considering these stocks.

data.title: Best of the week | What Sunil Mittal and Chandrababu Naidu told Mint, and what they left unsaid
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Best of the Week is a weekly newsletter by Siddharth Sharma/Shravani Sinha. Subscribe to Mint's newsletters to get them directly in your inbox.

This week, Mint conducted two major interviews with some of the most important people shaping India's economy, and a few of their answers surprised us. One of them involves a smile in response to a question about Mukesh Ambani. Another involves a first-of-its-kind law. Sunil Bharti Mittal and Chandrababu Naidu both opened up, and here is a glimpse of what they said.

Fifty years in business is a long time. Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises, the group that owns Airtel, marks the milestone this year. At 69, he is quick to dismiss any talk of a quiet ending.

We reminded him that he once said he would retire at 50. "No, not retire; I would never retire," he said. What he had meant, he explained, was politics or something away from business.

Then came a rare moment of candour. Could he do it all again, starting from nothing and building a $120 billion enterprise? "For me it's not going to be possible." Ground-up building, he says, takes a maniacal, no-weekends, no-family kind of determination. Professionals, in his view, can acquire and improve, but starting from ground zero is another matter.

The conversation turned sharper when we asked about tariffs. Airtel recently brought back its entry-level plan after a hike failed to attract followers. Mittal's explanation was, in a market this competitive, "you cannot stand alone beyond a point". But he doesn't think the problem is only about price. His real argument is about what India's digital future will demand. China has over a million towers; India has about 350,000. He believes India needs 600,000 to 700,000, and that the unlimited plans priced at Rs.400-500 are a "broken architecture" that can't afford it.

Then there is the AI bet. Airtel once sold minutes, then gigabytes. Tomorrow, Mittal says, the world will be tokens, and he has a plan for that. Billions of dollars are headed towards data centres, and he is even musing about offering customers a cheaper route to open-weight AI models. The balance sheet, he says, has never looked better, with the company debt-free by 2029 and buybacks possible.

There's much more. Mittal talks candidly about why satellite approvals are stuck, how he really felt when Jio arrived with a free year of service, and whether Airtel is heading to court over the AGR dues. We also asked him a question about Mukesh Ambani. His reaction began with a smile.

And then there's succession. His twin sons, his daughter and a company where he says he doesn't sign off on "10 paise" of spending. What he told us about who will eventually lead Bharti is worth reading in full.

If Mittal's story is about what has been built, Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu's is about what is being promised, and whether it will be kept.

In the last two years, investors have pledged as much as Rs.22.5 trillion to the state. But some have raised questions. Can a state with a strained fiscal position honour its incentives? And in a state famous for bruising politics, will policies survive the next election?

Naidu doesn't dodge. "I am pro-business," he says, arguing that wealth must come before welfare. He points to 50 amendments that decriminalize minor offences, wider automatic approvals and a promise of no political interference. Then he reveals something that could be a first for India. An Investment Protection Act, meant to ensure that a commitment made by one government can't be undone by another.

On the money question, he blames the previous government for the fiscal mess and says his government's credibility has pulled borrowing costs from 13% to below 9%. His answer for nervous investors is an escrow account, with incentive money set aside from tax collections so payments aren't delayed.

The numbers he shares are striking. About 73% of committed projects have won cabinet approval, and 54% have seen foundations laid. Now he's focused on start dates, and he rattles one off for Google's $15 billion AI data centre: 15 August 2028. At this week's CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, he plans to sign another Rs.9.5 trillion in investments, bringing the total to Rs.32 trillion. If it all comes through, he says, that means 2.5 million jobs.

Critics say the incentives are unsustainable. Naidu has a one-word reply: "marketing". He argues that the economic activity data centres draw in will repay the state many times over.

What's next for Andhra Pradesh? He lists steel, shipbuilding, green energy, quantum technology and more, and one of his ambitions involves turning Tirupati into something no Indian city is yet known for. He also cites a ranking that he says shows the investment drive reaching ordinary people, though whether the data backs him up is a debate worth having.

Delhi woke up to its annual grey blanket the morning after Diwali, and the air carried that familiar metallic sting. But the real shock was in the data. At several stations, readings climbed so high that monitors simply went blank for hours. How many data points vanished? More than you'd expect, and the share is rising. Delhi isn't alone. Over 200 cities saw air quality slide after the festivities, and the worst 24-hour reading didn't come from the capital at all. Where? We'll leave that for you.

The IPL could soon be bigger than the ten-team show fans know. The BCCI is weighing at least two new franchises from the 2028 media rights cycle, and Vadodara and Pune are in the frame, say people familiar with the plans. The price tag is what turns heads. One person in the know says each team could be valued at over $1 billion. Who is circling? A private equity firm, sovereign wealth funds and Indian conglomerates are said to be evaluating bids.

JSW Group has looked at India's airport business, and for now, it is staying on the ground. The Sajjan Jindal-led group has ruled out bidding in the government's latest privatization round after an internal review. The verdict? Airports, it concluded, are "a quasi-real estate play". Parth Jindal told Mint the business simply doesn't fit anything JSW already does. The 11 smaller airports on offer, he says, aren't viable for the group, and the big ones are already taken. But the door isn't fully shut.

In Delhi's Batla House, Mohammad Moin's joint family runs 8-10 mobile connections, yet his four school-going children do their homework on something else: a Rs.5 Wi-Fi sachet bought off a neighbour's router. No broadband bill, no long contract. Just six hours of internet for the price of a Parle-G. It sounds like the perfect fix for India's price-sensitive millions. So why has the government's flagship public Wi-Fi scheme managed only a sliver of its 10 million hotspot target? And why have many of the companies listed to run it gone quiet?

India Inc's corner offices are getting richer, and the rest of the building is noticing. A Mint analysis of 232 BSE 500 companies found that nearly 45% of executive heads earned more than 100 times their company's median employee pay in FY26, up from about 40% in FY20. The gap tells its own story. Director pay jumped 38% last year, while employee pay, excluding top executives, grew just 1%. Why the divergence? Experts point to a scarce pool of proven leaders, growing responsibilities and a big shift towards performance-linked pay.

Foreign capital is queuing up at the doors of India's NBFCs. Blackstone has just announced Rs.5,000 crore for roughly 16% of IIFL Finance, days after TPG's Rise Funds backed Arka Fincap. It follows bigger moves earlier this year, including a Japanese banking giant paying nearly Rs.40,000 crore for a stake in Shriram Finance. Why the rush? Credit demand is rising, governance has tightened, and a Fitch director says that shift matters enormously to foreign investors. Then there is the capital itself. What does fresh equity do to a lender's borrowing costs?

Elon Musk wants to make space launches dirt cheap by building rockets so big they can carry 100 tonnes in one go. India is betting on the opposite: small rockets, small satellites, rapid launches. SpaceX's logic is, fly often, carry plenty, and watch the cost per kilogram tumble. India's four-odd homegrown rockets, from Skyroot to Agnikul, carry around 500 kg each, a sliver of Starship's capacity. On paper, that looks like a mismatch.

For foreign investors, India has finally stopped being a painful bet. Between 30 October and 11 November, the Nifty 50 rose 11% in dollar terms, ahead of its 9.5% gain in rupee terms. Until 30 October, that gap ran the other way, with a weak rupee quietly eating into returns. Foreign investors have bought Rs.60,698 crore of Indian shares in just 11 days of November, the highest monthly inflow since December 2023. The rupee has recovered, and global markets are cooling off on a once-hot trade.

Just a month ago, Nvidia's Indian employees were sitting on a record windfall. Unvested shares held by staff were worth about $1.73 billion on 6 October, up from roughly $1.2 billion in March. Then the mood changed. First came worries over an AI slowdown, then a scandal around chief executive Jensen Huang and reports of Chinese spying. Hundreds of millions of dollars in paper gains have since melted away, by Mint's estimate. So are Nvidia's India staff panicking? A senior executive of over a decade says not quite, and has a theory about why.

The government's books look better than feared at the halfway mark, but don't let that fool you. Between April and September, the fiscal deficit hit 42.1% of the budget estimate, worse than last year's 36.5% yet still below the 50% mark. Capital spending didn't take a hit either. Who deserves the credit? Mostly dividends and disinvestment, which did the heavy lifting while tax collections lagged. That cushion is thinning, and in the last two years most of the deficit has shown up after September.

That's all from us this week. Subscribe to our newsletters and the website for what's in the news and beyond it. Write to us at newsletters@livemint.com.

data.title: Mars bets on India as a top-five growth market, targets $1.2 billion-plus revenue by 2030
data.description:
HYDERABAD, Nov. 14 -- Mars Inc., the American pet-care and snacking giant, wants India to become one of its five key "rapid growth" markets, betting on the country's expanding snacking and pet-care businesses to drive a sharp increase in revenue. India, already among Mars's top 20 markets, has significant room to grow, with the company targeting revenue of more than $1.2 billion by 2030.

"It really ought to be a top 5 market," Claus Aagaard, global chief financial officer of Mars, told Mint in an interview. The company's India revenue stood at around $600 million in 2025.

Mars is stepping up investments in manufacturing and technology to capture that opportunity. It operates seven factories in India and is investing Rs.1,500 crore in its Hyderabad pet-food facility. It has also partnered with IT services company Genpact to establish a global capability centre (GCC) in the city, which will support technology, analytics and process management across its global operations.

"This is a new strategic investment for us to drive innovation around technology and process management," Aagaard said on the sidelines of the GCC launch. The company also sees India as a source of engineering and technology talent that can be deployed across its global operations.

Pet-care is a key part of Mars's India growth strategy, even as competition intensifies with more domestic and international companies entering the market. Aagaard said the growing number of players reinforced his view that India was an attractive market for pet food.

"Competition is not a bad thing," he said. "When everybody wants to be here, it tells me.it confirms my hypothesis that the market is growing fast."

Over the past two years, large consumer goods companies including Reliance Consumer, Wipro Consumer Care, and Godrej Consumer Products have entered the pet-food market, launching packaged dog food and planning to expand into cat food.

Mars, meanwhile, is looking beyond packaged food to build a presence in veterinary services. In December 2024, it took a minority stake in Mumbai-based clinic chain Crown Veterinary Services. Aagaard said the company would take a gradual approach to expanding the business.

"I don't mind that it is a slow burn. We need to do this the right way and not overstretch it," he said.

Mars is also broadening its snacking portfolio following its $35.9 billion acquisition of Kellanova, completed in December 2025. The deal brought brands such as Pringles, Cheez-It and Pop-Tarts into its portfolio, extending its reach beyond established chocolate and gum brands including Snickers, M&M's and Twix.

The two businesses are being integrated under Mars's snacking division. Kellanova's portfolio and geographic presence complement Mars's existing operations, giving the company a broader platform across snacking categories and markets, Aagaard said.

The integration is still under way, with the company working to bring the organisations together. The Hyderabad GCC will support that effort, he said. "We are obviously busy putting these organizations together, setting it all up. So far, so good."

The opportunity extends beyond conventional snacks. Mars is looking to tap changing food habits through Tasty Bite, its ready-to-cook and business-to-business foods business, which sits within its food and nutrition division, separate from petcare and snacking.

In August 2017, Mars acquired Preferred Brands International, the US parent of Tasty Bite, securing a 74.23% controlling stake in its Indian subsidiary, Tasty Bite Eatables Ltd, which is listed on Indian stock exchanges.

Tasty Bite, which initially made Indian food for the US market, later expanded into ingredients for restaurants. Earlier this year, it launched consumer products in India, targeting shoppers seeking convenient meal options that require less cooking time, Aagaard said.

Competition for a share of India's snacking market is also drawing investor interest. Valued at more than Rs.50,000 crore, according to industry estimates, the market has attracted large global funds investing in domestic snack makers.

In December 2025, luxury fund L Catterton took a minority stake in namkeen and snacks maker Haldiram's. In January 2026, private equity fund General Atlantic acquired a stake in chips maker Balaji Wafers for an undisclosed amount. Meanwhile, candies, biscuits and snacks maker Parle Products is preparing for an initial public offering.

The GCC investment reflects a broader push by multinational consumer companies to build global technology and business operations in India.

L'Oreal is setting up a beauty-tech hub in Hyderabad to support global innovation, artificial intelligence, data analytics and supply-chain operations, while Nestle announced a GCC in the city in July. Starbucks has signed an agreement to establish a technology centre in Chennai, with plans to hire around 800 professionals. McDonald's opened its first India global office in Hyderabad in October 2025.

For Mars, the Hyderabad centre is intended to turn consumer data into growth opportunities in India and overseas. It will help the company identify shifts in consumer preferences, understand how shoppers discover and purchase products, and refine go-to-market strategies, particularly for newer channels such as quick commerce.

Tarun Chopra, unit leader, consumer goods, Genpact, cited quick commerce as an example of how the centre could use consumer data to improve the shopping experience. It can track the time consumers take to move from clicking on an app to completing a purchase. "That sometimes becomes 12 seconds. 12 seconds is too long," he said.

The reporter visited Mars's GCC facility in Hyderabad at the company's invitation.

data.title: Data recap: Nvidia's scrutiny, direct tax collections, IPL expansion
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- From governance concerns surrounding AI bellwether Nvidia to depleting reservoirs threatening India's agricultural output, corporate taxes outpacing non-corporate collections, a rise in mutual fund SIP stoppages and the BCCI exploring an expansion of the Indian Premier League (IPL), here are the key developments of the week in numbers.

Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday as the chief executive officer of Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia has been embroiled in controversy ever since Huang admitted to his extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore chip firm Megaspeed, reportedly identified by US intelligence agencies as a Chinese intelligence asset.

This prompted an independent probe by Nvidia's board, while Huang denied any knowledge of espionage. Amid the controversy, Nvidia shares slumped 10%, wiping billions off its market value. It has also drawn Nvidia into escalating US-China tensions.

Net direct tax collections rose 11.8% year-on-year to Rs.14.42 trillion as of 10 November, according to provisional data released by the Income Tax Department.

Taxes paid by non-corporates, led by individuals, continued to account for the largest share of collections. However, corporate tax and securities transaction tax (STT) collections grew faster, rising 18% and 51.6%, respectively.

The jump in STT collections comes amid a wider debate over capital market taxation in India, with the government reportedly considering changes to long-term capital gains tax and STT ahead of the Union Budget in February 2027.

Following a deficient monsoon, water levels in India's 178 reservoirs were 21% lower than a year earlier as of 5 November and about 17% below normal, Mint reported.

Reservoirs in southern India recorded the largest shortfall against normal storage levels, at 44%, followed by northern India at 24%. Low water levels have raised concerns over irrigation, agricultural output, food prices and hydropower generation.

The impact is also visible in the pace of rabi sowing. As of 6 November, wheat acreage was 12% lower year-on-year, while pulses and oilseeds were down 14% and 24%, respectively. Rice was the only major crop to record an increase, with acreage up 3%.

Rs.2-4 per litre: The amount by which Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices, citing higher procurement and fuel costs. Average retail prices have risen from Rs.55 in November 2022 to Rs.61 in October 2026.

Rs.62,370 crore: The fertilizer subsidy approved by the Centre for the ongoing rabi season, 64% higher than a year earlier. The higher allocation aims to keep input costs affordable for farmers amid volatile global prices.

Rs.5,000 crore: Blackstone's investment in non-banking financial company (NBFC) IIFL Finance for a 16% stake. Other NBFCs to attract foreign investment in 2026 include Manappuram Finance, Shriram Finance, and Sammaan Capital.

$7.1 billion: The net loss reported by Japan's SoftBank Group in the second quarter, its first quarterly loss in almost two years. This followed a $3.7 billion write-down related to its US data centre investments.

7: The average number of working days of paternity leave taken by Indian fathers, the lowest among the 12 major economies covered in a study by global hiring platform Deel. US fathers averaged 28 days.

The number of systematic investment plans (SIPs) discontinued in mutual funds exceeded new registrations in October, pushing the SIP stoppage ratio to 116%, the highest since April 2025, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (Amfi).

This was the second time in fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27) that the ratio crossed 100%, indicating that more SIPs were discontinued than started. Despite this, monthly SIP contributions remained close to their record levels in August and September. The first instance was in April 2026.

Equity mutual funds, however, saw net inflows fall 14% sequentially in October. While large-cap funds recorded higher inflows, mid-cap and small-cap funds saw declines.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is exploring plans to add at least two teams to the 10-franchise Indian Premier League (IPL) from the 2028 season, coinciding with the start of a new media rights cycle, Mint reported.

Pune and Vadodara have emerged as leading contenders, although discussions are at an early stage and the final choice of cities remains undecided. Each new franchise could command a valuation of more than $1 billion, amid strong investor interest.

The league last expanded ahead of the 2022 season, when Lucknow Super Giants and Gujarat Titans were added for $940 million and $750 million, respectively.

Although Pune and Vadodara are smaller markets than Mumbai and Bengaluru, IPL franchise valuations have risen at a compounded annual rate of 22-26% since the league's inception in 2007.

data.title: China's BYD clears import hurdle, looks to accelerate India push
data.description:
MUMBAI/NEW DELHI, Nov. 14 -- BYD India has secured regulatory certification for three of its four models, removing the annual 2,500-unit import restriction on those vehicles and giving the Chinese carmaker greater flexibility to meet demand. The move is particularly significant for its fast-selling Sealion 7, as BYD seeks to expand its presence in India's electric passenger vehicle market.

"We have four models and three of them are homologated with a certified agency, ARAI, except for Seal," Rajeev Chauhan, executive vice-president at BYD India, told Mint on the sidelines of the launch of the company's luxury brand Denza on Friday.

Homologation is the process through which testing agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) certify that a vehicle meets the country's technical and safety requirements for road use. Under India's import rules, vehicles with international certification but without Indian homologation can be imported only up to 2,500 units per model annually. Securing Indian homologation removes that restriction.

BYD was among a handful of foreign carmakers relying on international homologation certificates to sell vehicles in India, subjecting each model to the annual import ceiling. Most other foreign automakers have Indian homologation certificates, allowing them to import and sell vehicles without this restriction.

BYD entered India's electric passenger vehicle market in 2021 with the e6 electric MPV (multi-purpose vehicle), initially targeting fleet and commercial customers before expanding into the retail market. It launched the Atto 3 electric SUV (sport utility vehicle) in October 2022, followed by the Seal electric sedan in March 2024. In October 2024, it introduced the eMax 7, the successor to the e6, with six- and seven-seater configurations. Its fourth current offering, the Sealion 7 electric SUV, was launched in February 2025.

The certification is particularly significant for the Sealion 7, which has emerged as one of BYD's most important models in India, according to the company's disclosures. The carmaker had been working to secure Indian certification for the SUV after its import quota became a constraint on sales, Mint reported in March.

BYD's retail sales rose 54% to 5,361 electric passenger vehicles in fiscal year 2026 (FY26) from 3,481 in FY25, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). India's overall electric passenger vehicle market grew 83.6% to 199,923 units during the period, taking EV penetration to 4.2% from 2.6% a year earlier.

The certification comes as BYD seeks to regain a place among India's five largest electric passenger vehicle makers. It also comes as the company expands into the luxury segment with Denza.

BYD's expansion comes amid a gradual thaw in India-China relations. The two countries have resumed direct flights, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in September.

In March, the Centre eased certain provisions under Press Note 3, which had subjected investments from countries sharing a land border with India to government approval. The revised framework provides faster approvals for investments in select manufacturing sectors, but Chinese entities continue to face restrictions and the automobile sector remains outside the relaxation.

Earlier in March, the Centre had eased certain provisions under Press Note 3, which had made investments from countries sharing a land border with India subject to government approval. The revised framework provides a faster approval mechanism for investments in select manufacturing sectors. However, Chinese entities continue to face restrictions, and the automobile sector has not been brought under the wider relaxation.

The improving diplomatic climate has not removed the underlying commercial tensions. Indian companies continue to face difficulties in accessing Chinese technology and critical components, even as they try to build domestic capabilities.

Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, for instance, has been forced to develop its own lithium-ion cell technology capabilities after difficulties with technology transfers from its Chinese partner Gotion. JSW Group put its cell plans on hold after failing to secure a Chinese partner.

China's restrictions on rare-earth magnet exports in 2025 also disrupted Indian automakers and component suppliers.

Against this backdrop, BYD's expanded ability to import vehicles offers it a commercial advantage, even as it continues to sell completely built units and has no local assembly operations.

The company's latest move is to enter India's luxury car market through Denza, with two products: the D9, a seven-seater luxury MPV, and the Z9 GT. The brand will initially enter six cities: Mumbai, Gurugram, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad.

JSW MG Motor India, the joint venture between JSW Group and China's SAIC Motor, has also entered the electric luxury space with its M9 electric MPV and Cyberster sports car. Denza, however, is the first dedicated Chinese luxury brand to enter India.

BYD has yet to decide whether to seek Indian homologation for Denza's products. Chauhan said the company would first assess customer response. "We will look at the reactions of customers and the media, and only after that (take) a call on whether we should go in for certification," he said.

For now, BYD is counting on greater import flexibility for its existing models to build scale in India, while testing the market for its luxury offerings.

data.title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Groundstop that Upended Flights— WSJ
data.description:
By Alison Sider, Andrew Tangel and Jacob Passy

The Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide groundstop that halted departures for more than four hours Friday afternoon.

The hourslong groundstop upended travel for hundreds of thousands of people and the disruption is likely to ripple for days. Airlines canceled more than 6,000 flights Friday and have already scrubbed nearly 1,400 more on Saturday. Hundreds of flights either turned back or diverted as airports became gridlocked with too many planes on the ground and not enough room to park.

The problem started late Friday afternoon, as the FAA halted departures shortly before 4 p.m. ET, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns. More than 3,500 planes were in the air when the groundstop was issued.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said resuming flights would happen in a slow, controlled manner, with bigger planes with more passengers prioritized.

"What we have is an incredibly old air-traffic control system," Duffy said Friday in a press conference, blaming telecom routers that "actually got overloaded with data."

Duffy blamed "old hardware that went down" for the outage that lasted nearly five hours. He used the press conference at the White House to plead with Congress to approve funding to make upgrades, which he estimated to cost $50 billion: "We use 1980s little copper lines."

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House on Friday that there was "no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones."

Friday was on track to be one of the worst day of the year for air travel, outranked only by a sprawling winter storm in January that resulted in more than 11,600 cancellations, according to FlightAware.

More than 26,000 flights had been scheduled Friday, according to Cirium, an aviation data provider.

Even with the departure ban lifted, airlines were preparing for a difficult reset. Some had already scrubbed the vast majority of what they had planned to fly the remainder of Friday. Diversions and canceled flights left planes and crew members out of place for their next flights. That could create cascading scheduling problems into the weekend.

"It's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened," Duffy said.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom issues at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn't immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it is will work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved.

American said: "It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible.

Several airlines issued waivers to allow travelers to rebook flights without penalty. At some airports, including New York's LaGuardia, travelers whose flights were canceled had to wait in long lines to get their checked bags back before they could go home. At Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, security lines were empty as people milled about checking their phones for updates.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he was waiting in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Sara Garven, 66, was traveling with her husband home to Wisconsin from Sarasota, Fla., when the couple were stranded in Baltimore where they had a layover. Overhead announcements were being made roughly every 30 minutes, she said, but the information was no different from what was available online.

"Some are sprinkling the Friday the 13th component, which isn't really helping," she said. "Our main concern is just getting home safely."

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide groundstop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had only taken that step on Sept. 11, 2001.

Write to Alison Sider at alison.sider@wsj.com, Andrew Tangel at andrew.tangel@wsj.com and Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com

data.title: Tata Trusts Trustees Defend Tata Sons Listing, Question Leadership Delay
data.description:
Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have challenged Darius Khambata's objections to a public listing, arguing that governance and accountability, rather than ownership structure, preserve the Tata model

Tata Trusts Vice-Chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have defended the proposed stock market listing of Tata Sons, challenging fellow trustee Darius Khambata's argument that a public listing could threaten the Tata model, according to media reports.

In a five-page letter dated 11 November, the two trustees also questioned the handling of Tata Sons Executive Chairman N Chandrasekaran's reappointment and raised concerns over governance and decision-making within the Trusts.

The letter, addressed to Khambata, disputed his assessment of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) regulatory position and the events leading to the 17 September Tata Sons board meeting. The trustees argued that listing does not automatically weaken an institution's character, which they said depends on the quality of its governance and accountability.

Trustees Make Case For Listing

Srinivasan and Singh cited Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) as an example of a listed company operating under the influence of charitable trusts. They also referred to international companies controlled by foundations, arguing that public listing and long-term institutional objectives can coexist.

The two trustees said Tata Sons had engaged with the RBI on its regulatory status since 2023. This included repayment of debt and an application for deregistration submitted in March 2024.

They argued that the regulator's subsequent decision, following a review, that Tata Sons remained a systemically significant financial institution required to comply with the listing framework could not be attributed to inadequate engagement with the RBI.

The dispute intensified after the RBI rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its registration as a Core Investment Company in September 2026. The Tata Sons board subsequently backed steps towards a stock market listing at its 17 September meeting, despite opposition from Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata.

Seven-month Reappointment Delay

The letter also questioned the delay in Chandrasekaran's reappointment. The trustees said the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had unanimously recommended a five-year extension for him on 28 July 2025, but the decision was deferred in February 2026.

They questioned why the earlier unanimous recommendation had not been acted upon, resulting in seven months of uncertainty over the leadership of Tata Sons. The board eventually approved Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five years on 17 September.

Wider Governance Disagreement

Srinivasan and Singh also questioned whether opposition to listing was driven by concerns about preserving the Tata model or by the desire to retain control over Tata Sons within the current Trusts leadership. They argued that the interests of the charitable institutions and the governance responsibilities of the company's board needed to be considered separately.

Tata Trusts collectively hold around 66 per cent of Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata Group. Noel Tata and Khambata have opposed the proposed listing, maintaining that the holding company should remain privately held and that alternatives to comply with regulatory requirements should be explored.

data.title: Outlook Returns As Microsoft 365 Outage Exposes Enterprise Risks
data.description:
Microsoft's recovery efforts restore email access for users after a global disruption, while industry executives flag risks from dependence on a single technology provider

Microsoft Outlook began returning to service on Friday evening as Microsoft worked to restore its disrupted Microsoft 365 infrastructure, after a global outage affected email and workplace applications. The disruption exposed the operational risks of businesses relying on interconnected cloud-based services for communication, collaboration and daily operations.

Microsoft said service availability and email delivery were improving across an increasing portion of its affected infrastructure, although some users could continue to experience intermittent access issues and delayed messages. The disruption, which began on Thursday also affected Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Copilot and other services connected to Exchange Online.

Puneet Chandok, President of Microsoft India and South Asia, acknowledged the disruption in a LinkedIn post, saying, "We regret the disruption today's outage has caused for many of our customers. Our global teams continue to work with urgency to resolve the issue."

The outage has brought renewed attention to the dependence of businesses on a concentrated set of technology providers, with industry executives pointing to gaps in disaster recovery, alternative communication systems and infrastructure resilience.

Enterprise Operations Face Disruption

Microsoft 365 has evolved beyond an email platform, with businesses integrating Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and other applications into their daily operations. A disruption to interconnected services can affect internal communication, customer responses, approvals, meetings, and access to business documents.

Amit Singh, Practice Head, Managed Services, WeP Solutions, said the impact of such outages extends beyond messaging, as approvals can stall, customer responses get delayed, meetings and file access are disrupted, and decision-making slows down. "The core challenge is that enterprises have chosen deep integration for its simplicity, security and seamless collaboration. That same integration means a platform-wide disruption can have a far wider operational impact than most organisations anticipate, and there is rarely a ready fallback," he said.

The disruption also affected customer-facing operations in India. IndiGo reported that its email support services were impacted, temporarily affecting its ability to receive customer queries, while its other support channels remained operational. Air India said it had rerouted its email services to ensure customer queries continued to reach the airline without interruption. Both airlines said their flight operations were unaffected.

ICICI Lombard also issued a service advisory informing customers that its email support services were temporarily affected, while its website, IL TakeCare application and WhatsApp remained available.

Single-Provider Dependence Raises Concerns

The outage has highlighted the concentration risks associated with organisations relying on a single technology provider for multiple critical functions.

Govind Rammurthy, CEO and Managing Director of eScan, said dependence on a single cloud provider can create a single point of failure across business operations. "When core platforms go down simultaneously, organisations don't just lose email; they lose their entire operational backbone, communication, collaboration, compliance, and AI productivity in one stroke," he said.

Rammurthy said businesses need fallback communication channels, offline alternatives for critical workflows, and recovery procedures that are tested regularly. He also stressed that infrastructure resilience must receive as much attention as conventional cybersecurity defences. "The risk isn't always a threat actor, it's the architecture itself," he said.

Suneet Singh Thakur, Director – Cyber Resilience and Cybersecurity at Eventus Security, said businesses were adopting cloud platforms and AI-powered applications faster than their ability to withstand disruptions was evolving. He said large-scale outages could arise from software deployment errors, configuration changes, authentication failures, network disruptions or problems within shared infrastructure. In interconnected cloud environments, a failure in one component could potentially affect multiple services.

Thakur said enterprises should assess third-party dependencies, maintain alternative communication channels and establish recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO). Regular disaster recovery simulations, phased software rollouts, pre-production testing and automated rollback mechanisms were also important, he said.

Communication Continuity Remains A Gap

While Indian enterprises have made progress in disaster recovery for infrastructure, applications and data, communication continuity remains an overlooked area, according to Singh. He said maintaining an alternative email system was not as simple as keeping a backup because identity management, domains, security policies and user experience were closely interconnected.

Manoj Dhanda, Founder and CEO of Utho Cloud, said businesses should not assume that using a large global technology provider eliminates the need for contingency arrangements. "The provider's responsibility is to ensure that the service operates; however, it is the customer's responsibility to keep his business going," he said.

Dhanda said companies should maintain a second means of communication, secure backups, alternative access to critical data and tested recovery procedures. He added that cloud providers should roll out infrastructure changes gradually, maintain the ability to reverse them and distribute infrastructure geographically to limit the impact of failures.

Digital Sovereignty And Multi-Cloud Strategies

The disruption has also renewed questions around India's dependence on global technology providers for essential digital infrastructure. Sambratha Shetty, Chief Operating Officer of Synergia Foundation, said the concentration of organisational communication, data and workflows within a few interconnected platforms could create vulnerabilities for businesses and institutions.

She said digital sovereignty should not mean moving away from global technology providers, but retaining control over critical data, digital identities and essential infrastructure while ensuring viable alternatives are available. "Digital sovereignty should be about strategic autonomy and choice. India must be able to leverage global technology while ensuring that no single external provider becomes indispensable to the functioning of its critical institutions and economy," Shetty said.

For enterprises, the disruption has brought business continuity planning and infrastructure resilience into sharper focus, with experts emphasising the need to prepare for service failures rather than rely solely on providers to prevent them.

data.title: Nvidia Board Approaches Arm CEO Rene Haas As Potential Successor: Report
data.description:
The Nvidia board is considering several candidates for the top position, with Haas emerging as an external contender after leading Arm since 2022

Nvidia's board has approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Haas is among several candidates being considered for the position, although there is no certainty that he will receive an offer or accept the role.

The development comes a day after Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president and chief executive officer with immediate effect. The company's board has initiated a search for a permanent successor and said it would consider both internal and external candidates.

Haas Brings Nvidia Experience

Haas has led Arm, the UK-based semiconductor company backed by SoftBank, since 2022. He previously worked at Nvidia for approximately seven years, holding senior positions at the company before leaving more than a decade ago.

His earlier experience at Nvidia and continued relationships with Huang and some members of the company's board are understood to be among the factors behind his consideration, according to the FT report.

Arm declined to comment on the development, while Nvidia had not immediately responded to a request for comment, the report said.

Nvidia Begins Leadership Transition

Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive following Huang's resignation on 12 November. Kress will continue to hold the finance position while overseeing the company until a permanent successor is appointed.

In its announcement, Nvidia said the board would consider candidates from within and outside the company. It also appointed Harvey C. Jones as the board's first chair.

The leadership transition comes as Nvidia continues to play a central role in the global artificial intelligence industry through its graphics processing units and accelerated computing platforms. The choice of a permanent chief executive will therefore be closely watched by the semiconductor industry and investors.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk, Fundstrat’s Tom Lee, Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke and others have joined to sign a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia Corp. (NVDA).

Nvidia shares fell more than 2% in Friday’s regular trading, declining over 1% more during the afterhours session.

What The ‘Stand With Jensen’ Petition Is About

The petition, “Stand with Jensen,” had about 36,000 signatures at the time of writing. The tracker lists nearly 2,700 existing Nvidia employees among those who have signed it, while over 20,000 existing Nvidia shareholders are said to have been among those who have pledged support for Huang to be reinstated as the company’s chief.

“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too,” said Musk in a post on X.

The signatories said that Huang should be reinstated while an independent investigation into the allegations surrounding him establishes the facts.

In the open letter, the group praised Huang for spending 33 years building Nvidia, arguing that his leadership and contributions to the company deserve fairness and due process rather than an abrupt removal.

They also expressed concern that Huang was removed without meaningful due process, noting that they had not been presented with evidence substantiating allegations that the woman at the center of the controversy was a spy.

They urged the board to ensure an independent investigation, give Huang a fair opportunity to respond, disclose the inquiry's scope and timeline, and publicly explain the evidence and reasoning behind its decisions.

The letter emphasized that Huang should remain accountable, but argued that accountability must be based on evidence and a fair hearing.

Why Huang Stepped Down

Huang announced his decision to step down as Nvidia CEO, President, and a member of the board effective immediately on Thursday.

CFO Colette Kress has been appointed as the interim CEO while the company continues to search for a successor to Huang.

This came after reports revealed details about Huang’s extramarital affairs, including those with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset and an executive reporting directly to him.

data.title: HUDCO, PFC, Others Raise Over 10k cr Via Bond Sales
data.description:
Rozebud Gonsalves Mumbai: The corporate bond market saw three large issuances on Friday, raising a combined 8,441 crore, as issuers stepped up borrowings amid softer yields. State-owned HUDCO raised 2,500 crore through 10-year bonds, while PFC accepted 2,968 crore for 18-month bonds and 2,973 crore for five-year papers. Along with these three, Tata Capital Housing Finance, Nirmal Bang Securities and others issued smaller papers. "The HUDCO paper was likely presold, there were only three large bids which included LIC and EPFO, as this was a longer tenured paper.

It is because of this that their rate was below 8%," said a corporate bond dealer at a private firm. HUDCO was able to get a rate of 7.92% for their 10 year paper, while the Power Finance Corporation paper for 18 months and 5 years had rates of 8.21% and 8.05% respectively. The 10-year benchmark government bond yield rose 4 bps from its previous close to settle at 7.29% on Friday.

While the yield has edged up from around 7.15% levels seen last week, it remains below the 7.50% high recorded in October, according to CCIL data. A relatively softer benchmark yield and expectations of a rate hike in December has prompted a rush of corporate bond issuances of the past few weeks. Tata Capital Housing Finance raised 753 crore, while Nirmal Bang Securities raised 50 crore. These two issuances, along with a few other smaller bonds takes the single day aggregate to over 10,000 crore.

data.title: Grasim Ind's Q2 Profit Triples, Revenue up 33%
data.description:

The revenue growth was led by continued growth momentum across the company's core and growth businesses, the company said, as key businesses such as cellulosic fibres, chemicals and textiles remained resilient despite global volatility, while the paints and B2B e-commerce businesses saw strong consumer and brand traction.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) rose 158% year-on-year to 4,615 crore, supported by a dividend income of 3,968 crore from UltraTech Cement and a favourable product mix, partially offset by higher input prices. "We believe that for this quarter, standalone results reflect actual underlying performance of the company, as compared to consolidated results," the company said in a statement. "The dividend from UltraTech of 3,968 crore is cash received by the company, which is accounted for in standalone results, however, gets eliminated in consolidated results," it said.

In its cellulosic fibres business, the company's revenue grew 29% year-on- year to 5,344 crore aided by volume growth, a favourable product mix and stable domestic realisations. This helped offset the impact of geo-political issues and higher input and logistics costs, the company said. EBITDA from the business rose 49% year-on-year to 522 crore. In its chemicals business, the company's revenue rose 15% year-on-year to 2,759 crore, while EBITDA fell 11% to 326 crore, due to higher power costs in the caustic soda business and lower profitability in the specialty chemicals business. Its decorative paints business 'Birla Opus' saw a 35% yoy growth in revenue to 1,337 crore, while volume growth stood at 20%.

data.title: Crude Shock, Inflation Sting End D-Street's Winning Run
data.description:
Sensex slips 0.39%, Nifty down 0.61%, end the week with gains Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian benchmark indices snapped a three-session winning streak on Friday as rising crude oil prices and a sharper-than-expected increase in retail inflation weighed on investor sentiment. Inflationary concerns and the possibility of a rate increase at the next monetary policy review dented D-Street sentiment.

The BSE Sensex fell 318.56 points, or 0.39%, to close at 81,592.45, while the NSE Nifty50 declined 155.05 points, or 0.61%, to 25,144.30. Despite Friday's decline, the benchmarks ended the week with gains. The Sensex rose 0.7%, while the Nifty gained 0.45%. Brent crude futures climbed to around $95.5 a barrel from nearly $92, as escalating attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz threatened global oil supplies.

Investor concerns intensified after India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, crossing the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years. "The market's risk environment has become more complicated towards the end of the week with October retail inflation rose to 6.09%, moving above the RBI's upper tolerance band, while food inflation accelerated to 8.94%, raising concerns about the interest-rate outlook and household consumption," said Gaurav Garg, head -research, Lemonn.

He also said sustained increase in crude prices could put pressure on India's current account, the rupee, corporate input costs and inflation, potentially offsetting some of the benefits of foreign fund inflows. "Looking ahead, our near-term view remains cautiously positive, but we expect markets to undergo consolidation with intermittent volatility rather than continue moving higher in a straight line," Garg said.

Sectorally, realty, auto and cement stocks witnessed the sharpest selling pressure. Banking, financial services and metal shares also weighed on the benchmarks. Broader markets also ended lower, though losses were relatively contained. Both Nifty Midcap 150 Index and Nifty Smallcap 250 Index 0.3% each. In the last one week, Nifty Midcap 150 index has gained 1.84%, while Nifty Small Cap 250 Index went up 3.19%. The India VIX, a measure of market volatility, fell nearly 5.06%, indicating a moderation in expectations of near-term market volatility. "A decisive breach below 24,850 could accelerate selling pressure and expose the index to a further decline towards the 24,600 mark in the near term," said Sudeep Shah, head - Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities.

data.title: Cruise Mode: Cars Sales Race to October Best
data.description:
2w & 3w sales also remain healthy amid strong demand Our Bureau New Delhi: Domestic car sales accelerated 12.4% year-on-year to a record high in October as manufacturers rushed stock to dealerships ahead of the Dhanteras and Diwali festivals. Demand for two-wheelers also remained buoyant, pointing to robust appetite among entry-level buyers during the festive period.

Figures released by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) show that 519,060 hatchbacks, sedans and utility vehicles were sold in October, compared with 461,614 units sold in the year-ago period. The previous sales record was set in October 2025, after the goods and services tax rate cuts. "Indian automobile industry continues to witness healthy demand momentum. The passenger vehicle segment achieved its strongest-ever October performance, crossing the significant milestone of 500,000 units in monthly sales," said Rajesh Menon, director general, SIAM. Major manufacturers-Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors PV, Mahindra & Mahindra, Hyundai Motor and Kia India-all posted their highest-ever monthly figures.

Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer (market and sales), Maruti Suzuki, said, "This is the highest-ever sales we have recorded in a month in the domestic market since inception. We have seen strong growth across categories, be it small cars or SUVs (sport utility vehicles)." Two-wheeler sales also increased sharply in October, up 16.1% year-on-year to 2,577,810 units.

Growth was largely fuelled by scooters, where volume surged 31.6% to 1,096,756 units. Motorcycle sales rose 6.6% to 1,423,118 units. "In the two-wheeler segment, demand continues to be supported by improved credit availability and replacement demand, across both rural and urban markets. For three-wheelers, last-mile mobility requirements and rapid electrification remain strong structural drivers. Overall, the demand outlook remains positive," Menon added. Three-wheeler sales increased 25.7% year-on-year to 103,349 units last month.
